subject: project:gdl
value: EXTERNCHECK WIDENED + IMAGE-WIDE EXTERN DEFECT TABLE (2026-08-31). WHAT WAS BLIND. The old tools/gdl/externcheck.py flagged a symbol only when its declared-type set mixed a float class with an int class, and it explicitly demoted pointer-vs-int to --all as 'benign word traffic'. It was therefore structurally incapable of seeing three defect classes that later waves rediscovered by hand: u32-vs-s32 (both collapsed to class 'int'), pointer-vs-int (suppressed by design), and - the largest hole - FUNCTION PROTOTYPES, because its regex required a `;` immediately after the declarator, so `extern void *FindClosestWaypoint(f64 maxDist, f32*, s32)` never matched at all. The f64-vs-f32 defect that attempt.findclosestwaypoint-param-width-sets-slot-floor-exact.20260901.v1 had to find by hand was thus invisible to the very tool meant to catch it. WHAT IT DOES NOW. Every declaration is reduced to a canonical class (s8/u8/s16/u16/s32/u32/s64/u64/f32/f64/void, ptr->pointee, agg:<name>), ANY disagreement is reported, and each line carries a CLASS column next to the original type text (output format otherwise unchanged). Prototypes are scanned separately and compared on return type plus per-parameter class. Three severities: CONFLICT (conclusive scalar/pointer split - fix), HAZARD (`int` vs `s32` only - per-site gamble, gate each), REVIEW (an unknown/aggregate typedef is involved - needs judgment). Exit 1 on any CONFLICT. THE TABLE. Object externs: 100 CONFLICT, 43 HAZARD, 26 REVIEW. The conclusive 100 break down as pointer-vs-int 46, signedness 28, width 22, float-vs-nonfloat 4 - i.e. 96 of 100 are in classes the old tool could not report, and only 4 are the class it was written for. Prototypes: 272 splits, of which 225 have IDENTICAL ARITY and are the high-signal set; the other 47 differ in argument COUNT and are mostly the project's deliberate K&R-passthrough idiom, so arity-differing rows must NOT be batch-'fixed'. FIXED THIS PASS, all byte-identical: FindClosestWaypoint f64 -> f32 in critter.c:326 and tower.c:58 (tower ALSO required dropping the now-redundant `(f64)` cast at tower.c:1738 - with the cast left in place the change was not byte-identical and aborted on the SumnerDoSpeech webfrank pin, which is a useful tell that a redundant cast is doing real work); gBossObj u32 -> u8* in main.c:143 (3 other TUs already say u8*, and main.c only null-tests it); sPowerupsBuf u32 -> void* in options.c:293 (include/game/item.h is the canonical declaration and the sole use was already `(void*)sPowerupsBuf`). HIGHEST-VALUE QUEUE LEFT, and it is the same class that just produced an exact match: ELEVEN same-arity prototype splits mix f32 and f64 - DistanceToClosestPlayer, FloorPos, MBAddLight, NormalVector2D, Random, SlowNormalVector, __cvt_fp2unsigned, atan2, cos, mbBlitCvtCoord, sin. Each is a candidate FindClosestWaypoint: a wrong f64 parameter inflates the callee's parameter save area and moves its whole local-block floor, which is invisible in the opcode stream and shows up only in slotdiff. Work these with slotdiff, not fndiff. NOT FIXED, with reason: sItemFile1Buf (boss.c:140 `int` vs item.h `void*`) is COUPLED - boss.c also declares `extern int InitCustomEffect(int buf, ...)`, so the object's type and its consumer's prototype must move together; sMusicTrackHi, lbl_80282930, opt_force_player, sSpecialItem10, gTextFormatBuf, lbl_80112370, lbl_8011B578 and the remaining single-site-minority rows are listed by the tool and need per-symbol ground truth (symbols.txt size/type or target asm) before editing. CAUTION carried from the corpus: the 43 HAZARD rows are NOT a chore list - claim.law.int-vs-signed-long-extern-reorders-schedule.20260831.v1 shows the same edit to the same symbol can be byte-identical in one TU and cost 12 real lines in another.
